title: Compatible scheme modules give a quasi-coherent sheaf on a fibred fppf site
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:\mathcal C\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Give its big fppf site the structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(x)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ for $x\in\mathcal C(T)$, with the site and module quasi-coherence conventions of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. For each such $x$ suppose given a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-module $M_x$ [pqf-def-coherent]. For every arrow $\alpha:y\to x$ over $u:T'\to T$, suppose given an isomorphism $\theta_\alpha:u^*M_x\xrightarrow{\sim}M_y$, where $u^*$ is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume $\theta_{\mathrm{id}_x}=\mathrm{id}_{M_x}$ and, for composable $\beta:z\to y$ over $v:T''\to T'$, $\theta_{\alpha\circ\beta}=\theta_\beta\circ v^*\theta_\alpha$ under $(u\circ v)^*\simeq v^*u^*$. Then the presheaf $F(x)=\Gamma(T,M_x)$, whose restriction along $\alpha$ pulls a section to $u^*M_x$ and applies $\theta_\alpha$, is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules for the fppf topology and is quasi-coherent in the local-presentation sense. No algebraicity, finiteness or representability assumption on $\mathcal C$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), cartesian criterion and its proof, with Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent). The statement writes the associated section presheaf explicitly, using the scheme associated-module construction invoked in that proof.

proof.text: Put $\rho_\alpha(s)=\Gamma(T',\theta_\alpha)(u^*s)$. In the tensor definition [def-pc-module-pullback], section pullback sends the germ of $s$ to $1\otimes s$; hence it is additive, semilinear for pullback of functions, and natural in module maps. Two successive pullbacks give $1\otimes(1\otimes s)$, identified with $1\otimes s$ for the composite. The assumed identity and cocycle equations for $\theta$ therefore give $\rho_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{\alpha\beta}=\rho_\beta\rho_\alpha$. With the pointwise $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$-actions this is exactly an $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module presheaf [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra].

source.place: Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), converse proof; Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent), sufficiency; section-restriction, lemma-localizing.

proof.text: Fix $x\in\mathcal C(T)$. The functor $p_x:\mathcal C/x\to\mathit{Sch}/T$ sends $(\alpha:y\to x)$ to $u=p(\alpha)$. It is essentially surjective because every base arrow to $T$ has a lift to $x$. For two such lifts, every base triangle has a unique arrow above it by the defining factorization property of a category fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Thus $p_x$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Covers on both sides are precisely the families whose base maps are fppf covers [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], and the structure rings are the same $\Gamma(T',\mathcal O_{T'})$. We can therefore describe the ringed slice using $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$.

source.place: Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), converse proof; Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent), sufficiency; section-restriction, lemma-localizing.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence], $A_T(M_x)(u:T'\to T)=\Gamma(T',u^*M_x)$ with section-pullback restrictions (through $v^*u^*M_x\simeq(uv)^*M_x$) is a quasi-coherent module sheaf on the big fppf site of $T$. On the slice its comparison with $F$ is explicitly $\lambda_\alpha=\Gamma(T',\theta_\alpha):A_T(M_x)(p_x\alpha)=\Gamma(T',u^*M_x)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T',M_y)=F(y)$ for $\alpha:y\to x$ over $u$; $\lambda_{\mathrm{id}_x}=\mathrm{id}$ since $\theta_{\mathrm{id}_x}=\mathrm{id}$. For a slice arrow $\beta:z\to y$ over $v:T''\to T'$ (so $z$ lies over $x$ via $\alpha\beta$ over $uv$) and an arbitrary section $t\in\Gamma(T',u^*M_x)$, not only one of the form $u^*s$, the two composites are $\rho_\beta(\lambda_\alpha(t))=\Gamma(T'',\theta_\beta)\big(v^*\Gamma(T',\theta_\alpha)(t)\big)$ and $\lambda_{\alpha\beta}(v^*t)=\Gamma(T'',\theta_{\alpha\beta})(v^*t)$, with $v^*t$ read in $(uv)^*M_x$. Naturality of section pullback in module maps (step 1) gives $v^*\Gamma(T',\theta_\alpha)(t)=\Gamma(T'',v^*\theta_\alpha)(v^*t)$, and the assumed cocycle equation $\theta_{\alpha\beta}=\theta_\beta\circ v^*\theta_\alpha$ identifies the two. Module operations are respected because each $\Gamma(\theta_\alpha)$ is $\Gamma(T',\mathcal O_{T'})$-linear. Thus $\lambda$ is an isomorphism of module presheaves on $\mathcal C/x\simeq(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$, including the specified restrictions, not merely an objectwise bijection.

source.place: Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), converse proof; Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent), sufficiency; section-restriction, lemma-localizing.

proof.text: For an fppf covering $\{y_i\to x\}$, a matching family for $F$ is the same matching family for $F|_{\mathcal C/x}$: its compatibility is tested on arrows into the $y_i$ over $x$. Step 3 identifies this restricted presheaf with a sheaf, so the family has a unique amalgamation in $F(x)$. As $x$ and its cover were arbitrary, $F$ is a sheaf. The module operations already commute with restrictions by step 1; hence this is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules with the original values.

source.place: Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), converse proof; Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent), sufficiency; section-restriction, lemma-localizing.

proof.text: On each ringed slice, step 3 identifies $F$ with the quasi-coherent sheaf $A_T(M_x)$, where site quasi-coherence means local presentations by arbitrary small free modules. By the explicit definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], choose such a covering of the terminal object $\mathrm{id}_T$ and its free presentations. Under step 2 these are covers $y_i\to x$ and the same presentations on $\mathcal C/y_i$, with ring sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}|_{\mathcal C/y_i}$. This supplies exactly the required local presentations at each $x$. No property of $\mathcal C$ beyond the lift and unique-factorization axioms was used.
